newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 20.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.09 (+0.37)

Mobil Corp said on Thursday its Mobil Exploration and Development Argentina Inc (MEDA) unit had bought about a 28 percent interest in Argentina's Sierra Chata gas field and Chihuidos block from BHP Petroleum. BHP's first quarter results are also expected before midday (0200 GMT) and copper prices were firmer overnight.

Toro Co said on Thursday in the United States it has agreed to buy the James Hardie Irrigation Group from Australia-based James Hardie Industries Ltd for about US$130 million. James Hardie Industries Ltd said later on Friday that the US$130 million raised from the sale of its global irrigation business would be used to expand its fibre cement building products operations, particularly in the United States.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Monday, without attribution, that Coles Myer Deputy Chairman Solomon Lew was threatening to take legal action against Coles Myer. The newspaper also said Coles' non-executive directors had accelerated plans to remove chief executive Peter Bartels. A spokesman for Coles Myer was not immediately available for comment.

Shell Australia Ltd chief executive Roland Williams told Reuters Shell wants to integrate the huge North West Shelf and Gorgon gas projects off northwest Australia and that talks with its partners would soon enter a "constructive" phase. Shell, a part owner in each project, dismissed as absurd the option of developing Gorgon as a stand-alone project with its own greenfield liquified natural gas plant, and said it was working to jointly develop Gorgon and the North West Shelf. Woodside is a one-sixth partner in the North West Shelf project.

The Australian government privately supported a new system of media ownership rules which would limit the amount of the total media market any one proprietor could own, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday.

Ballarat Brewing Co Ltd said on Friday it had been told by the Australian Securities Commission that the application by Guiness Peat Group Plc to make a full bid for the tourism and leisure group had been unsuccessful.
Leighton Holdings Ltd said late on Thursday its Indonesian subsidiary PT Theiss Contractors Indonesia in a joint venture with Kopnatel has been awarded an A$200 million telecomunications contract.
